science.label: WHY HYDROGEN
science.intro: Hydrogen water attracts big claims. Here we separate the myths from the facts, and show what researchers have actually studied, honestly and in plain words.

intro: You've probably heard about hydrogen water. But did you know your gut makes hydrogen every day, and your breath carries it out? Here's what molecular hydrogen is, what it does in your body, and why it has caught the attention of researchers around the world.

ch2.title: Free radicals, and the art of balance
ch2.intro: To understand why hydrogen interests researchers, it helps to start with something that happens in your body every second.

steps.title: Every breath, every heartbeat
steps.text: Your cells use oxygen to make energy. That process naturally creates by-products called free radicals: unstable molecules that react quickly with whatever is around them.

steps.title: Everyday life adds more
steps.text: Hard training, strong sun, air pollution, stress and short nights all increase the number of free radicals your body has to deal with.

steps.title: Not all bad
steps.text: In small amounts, free radicals are useful. Your cells use them as signals, for example to adapt and grow stronger after exercise.

steps.title: Your built-in defenses
steps.text: Your body keeps free radicals in check with its own antioxidant enzymes, such as superoxide dismutase and glutathione, helped by antioxidants from food.

steps.title: When the balance tips
steps.text: When free radicals outpace your defenses for a long time, scientists call it oxidative stress. They can then damage fats, proteins and DNA in cells. That’s why researchers study oxidative stress in relation to how we recover, how we age and how we feel.

steps.title: Where hydrogen fits
steps.text: This is where hydrogen comes in. It doesn't replace your defenses. Research suggests it supports them, helping your body's own antioxidant systems do their work.*

ch2.closing: Oxidative stress is part of being alive. That’s why so much research focuses on it, and why hydrogen is being studied in so many areas. A daily glass of hydrogen water is a simple way to support your body’s own antioxidant defenses, from the ground up.*

ch3.title: What hydrogen does: two ideas
ch3.intro: Researchers are still working out exactly how hydrogen works in the body. Two ideas lead the way, and they point in the same direction.

ideas.title: A selective antioxidant
ideas.text: The first studies suggested that hydrogen reacts mainly with the most aggressive free radicals, while leaving the useful signalling ones alone. That would make it different from many antioxidants, which act on everything they meet.

ideas.title: A gentle signal
ideas.text: Newer research suggests hydrogen does even more as a messenger. It seems to nudge cells to switch on their own defense systems, including the ones that make the body’s antioxidant enzymes. In this view, hydrogen doesn’t do the work for your body. It helps your body do it better.

ch1.title: What is molecular hydrogen?
ch1.text: Molecular hydrogen, or H₂, is simply two hydrogen atoms joined together. It’s the smallest molecule in the universe: a gas with no color, smell or taste.
ch1.h2Caption: H₂, molecular hydrogen: free to move.
ch1.waterCaption: H₂O, water: the hydrogen is bound to oxygen.
ch1.note: Hydrogen water is ordinary water with extra H₂ gas dissolved in it. That dissolved H₂ is what researchers study.

cards.title: The smallest of all
cards.text: Because it’s so tiny, hydrogen passes easily through cell membranes and can reach every part of the cell.

cards.title: Already part of you
cards.text: Your gut bacteria make hydrogen every day as they digest fiber. Some of it even ends up in your breath.

cards.title: A growing field
cards.text: Scientific interest took off after a 2007 paper in Nature Medicine. Since then, researchers have published well over a thousand studies on molecular hydrogen.

more.q: How does hydrogen get into water?
more.a: Hydrogen gas dissolves in water, much like the bubbles in sparkling water. A bottle can make it fresh by electrolysis, and a tablet can make it in your glass through a reaction of magnesium with water. Because it’s so small, hydrogen slowly escapes from water, which is why it’s best made fresh and drunk soon.

more.q: Is hydrogen water the same as alkaline water?
more.a: No. The research is about the dissolved hydrogen gas, not the pH. Hydrogen water can be neutral, slightly alkaline or slightly acidic, depending on how it’s made.

Hydrogen gas has GRAS status (‘generally recognized as safe’) for use in drinking water and beverages. In 2014, the FDA reviewed a GRAS notice for hydrogen gas in drinking water, flavored drinks and soft drinks, and had no questions. Hydrogen is also something your body already knows: your gut bacteria make it every day. In human studies, hydrogen water has been well tolerated.

ch6.title: Why fresh matters
ch6.intro: Hydrogen is the smallest molecule there is. That's what makes it interesting, and it's also why it doesn't stay in water for long.

blocks.title: Small enough to slip away
blocks.text: Because hydrogen is so tiny, it gradually escapes from water, especially from an open glass. It can even slip through many types of plastic, which is why ready-made hydrogen water tends to lose strength while it sits on a shelf.

blocks.title: So make it fresh
blocks.text: The simplest answer is to make hydrogen water right before you drink it. That's the idea behind both H2 | 4 YOU products: the One makes it fresh in the bottle, and Fizz makes it fresh in your glass.

ppbText: The amount of hydrogen dissolved in water is measured in parts per billion (ppb). 1,000 ppb equals 1 part per million (ppm), or 1 milligram of hydrogen in a liter of water. It's measured with a dissolved hydrogen meter or special test drops. An ORP reading doesn't measure it (see

ch6.ppbClosing: Higher isn't automatically better. How much you drink, how often and how fresh it is matter just as much.

ch6.amountTitle: Concentration isn't the same as amount
ch6.amountText: A ppb number tells you how concentrated the hydrogen is, not how much of it you actually drink. For that, you need to look at milligrams per serving.

amountCards.label: The One, in numbers
amountCards.text: At 5,000 ppb, water holds 5 mg of hydrogen per liter. One bottle holds 290 ml (9.8 fl oz), so a full bottle gives you about 1.45 mg (about 0.7 mg at 2,500 ppb). To drink 5 mg, you'd need about 3½ bottles, roughly one liter.

amountCards.label: Why tablet numbers vary
amountCards.text: A tablet makes a set amount of hydrogen. Dissolve it in a small glass and the ppb number looks high. Use a larger glass and the number drops, but you drink about the same amount of hydrogen. That's why milligrams per serving is the fairer way to compare.

studies.title: Hydrogen-rich water improved ventilatory, perceptual and lactate responses to exercise
studies.line: At high intensity, after one serving before exercise.
studies.citation: Botek et al. · Int J Sports Med · 2019
studies.did: 12 healthy men drank 600 ml of hydrogen-rich water or placebo water within 30 minutes before a cycling test of rising intensity.
studies.found: Blood lactate was lower at the highest intensities (8.9 vs 10.6 mmol/L), and the effort felt slightly easier.
studies.note: A small study in young men, testing a single serving.

studies.title: Effects of 8 days intake of hydrogen-rich water on muscular endurance performance and fatigue recovery
studies.line: More repetitions in a strength-endurance test.
studies.citation: Zhou et al. · Frontiers in Physiology · 2024
studies.did: 18 trained young men drank hydrogen-rich water or placebo water for 8 days, then did six sets of half-squats.
studies.found: They completed more repetitions (78 vs 70) and produced more total power than with placebo.
studies.note: Recovery from soreness over the next two days was no different.

studies.title: Effects of drinking hydrogen-rich water on muscle fatigue in elite athletes
studies.line: Strength held up better early in a hard test.
studies.citation: Aoki et al. · Medical Gas Research · 2012
studies.did: 10 male soccer players drank 1.5 liters of hydrogen-rich water or placebo water, then cycled hard for 30 minutes and did 100 maximal knee extensions.
studies.found: Blood lactate rose less during heavy exercise, and muscle strength didn't drop in the early part of the test, as it did with placebo.
studies.note: A small pilot study. Blood markers of oxidative stress didn't change.

studies.title: Molecular hydrogen and exercise-induced oxidative stress in healthy adults: a meta-analysis
studies.line: When the results of six studies were combined.
studies.citation: Li et al. · Frontiers in Nutrition · 2024
studies.did: Researchers combined six studies with 76 healthy adults who used hydrogen around exercise, as hydrogen water, a hydrogen bath or inhaled hydrogen.
studies.found: The body's antioxidant capacity in blood was higher with hydrogen than with placebo (p = 0.03).
studies.note: Markers of oxidative stress themselves didn't change. No study lasted longer than 14 days.

studies.title: Hydrogen-rich water in healthy adults: a randomized, double-blind, controlled trial
studies.line: Antioxidant capacity rose more in adults over 30.
studies.did: Healthy adults aged 20 to 59 drank 1.5 liters of hydrogen-rich water or plain water every day for four weeks.
studies.found: Antioxidant capacity rose more in participants aged 30 and over, and immune cells showed calmer activity.
studies.note: Across all ages together, oxidative stress markers didn't differ between the groups.

studies.title: Six months of hydrogen-rich water in adults aged 70 and over
studies.line: After six months, in adults over 70.
studies.did: 40 adults aged 70 and over drank half a liter of hydrogen-rich water or a control drink every day for six months.
studies.found: Chair-stand performance improved more than in the control group, and telomere length held steady while it shortened in the control group.
studies.note: A small pilot study. Most other measures showed no difference.

studies.title: Six weeks of hydrogen-rich water during resistance training in adults over 50
studies.line: In adults over 50 starting strength training.
studies.citation: Kuzmanovic et al. · Research in Sports Medicine · 2025
studies.did: 27 adults aged 50 to 65, new to exercise, drank hydrogen-rich water or regular water for six weeks during a strength training program.
studies.found: Markers of muscle damage after training were lower than with regular water.
studies.note: Strength gains were no different between the groups.

studies.title: Six weeks of hydrogen-rich water during resistance training in adults over 50
studies.line: In 5 of 7 areas measured, after six weeks.
studies.citation: Kuzmanovic et al. · Research in Sports Medicine · 2025
studies.did: The same 27 adults aged 50 to 65 rated their sleep before and after six weeks of hydrogen-rich water or regular water.
studies.found: Sleep quality improved in 5 of the 7 areas measured. The regular-water group showed no change.
studies.note: Sleep was a secondary measure in a small pilot study.

studies.title: Hydrogen-rich water for mood, anxiety and autonomic nerve function in daily life
studies.line: Better mood in everyday life, after four weeks.
studies.citation: Mizuno et al. · Medical Gas Research · 2017
studies.did: 26 healthy adults drank 600 ml of hydrogen-rich water or placebo water a day, four weeks each.
studies.found: Scores for mood and anxiety improved more than with placebo, and resting nerve activity linked to stress was lower.
studies.note: A small study based partly on how people said they felt.

ch4.title: Myth or fact?
ch4.intro: Hydrogen water attracts big claims, and a few mix-ups. Here's what holds up, and what doesn't.
ch4.listToggle: See all myths as a list

cards.fact: All water contains hydrogen, but there it's bound to oxygen. Hydrogen water also carries dissolved H₂ gas: the free, tiny molecule that researchers study.

cards.myth: It's the alkalinity that does the work.
cards.fact: The research is about dissolved hydrogen, not pH. Hydrogen water can be neutral, slightly alkaline or slightly acidic, depending on how it's made.

cards.myth: Hydrogen water is related to hydrogen peroxide.
cards.fact: They're completely different. Hydrogen peroxide (H₂O₂) is a strong oxidizer used for bleaching and cleaning. Molecular hydrogen (H₂) is a gentle, stable gas.

cards.myth: A negative ORP reading tells you how much hydrogen is in the water.
cards.fact: ORP is influenced by many things, such as pH and minerals. Only a dissolved hydrogen measurement, in ppb or ppm, tells you how much hydrogen is really there.

Research suggests it's more selective than that. Hydrogen seems to react mainly with the most aggressive free radicals, and to act as a gentle signal that helps the body's own defenses. Read more in Hydrogen 101.

cards.myth: All the research has been done in animals.
cards.fact: Much of the early research was, but hundreds of human studies have now been published, and new ones appear every year.
Concentration matters, but so do how much you drink, how often, and how fresh it is. Researchers are still working out the ideal daily amount.

cards.myth: Hydrogen is explosive, so hydrogen water can't be safe.
cards.fact: Hydrogen gas is only flammable at high concentrations in air. The amount dissolved in a glass of water is far below that, and hydrogen gas has GRAS status for use in drinking water and beverages.
No. Hydrogen is not a cure for anything, and it's no replacement for medical care. It's a simple daily habit that research suggests may support your body's own antioxidant defenses.*
